**Finding: IP — Compliant (meets preferred).**

The document satisfies every preferred element:

| Element | Where |
|---|---|
| Customer owns Deliverables/work product | § 14.2 ("Upon creation … Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer") |
| Vendor assigns | § 14.2 ("Vendor hereby assigns … all worldwide right, title, and interest") |
| Vendor retains pre-existing IP | § 14.3 + § 1.8 definition of Vendor Technology |
| Perpetual / irrevocable / royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor IP | § 14.3 routing to § 13.2 ("perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence") |
| Customer retains all rights in Customer Data | § 14.1 |
| Vendor Customer Data licence limited to providing Services | § 14.1 ("solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer"), reinforced by § 15.1's no-sale/no-advertising/no-model-training consent gate |
| No joint ownership | § 14.4 |

The § 14.1 processing right is service delivery for us (provide, secure, support, improve the Services **for Customer**), not independent exploitation, so it does not need narrowing. The § 15.1 "without Customer's express written consent" wording is a consent gate, not a standing Vendor licence.

Only non-material observations, noted rather than redlined: Deliverable ownership in § 14.2 is expressed as "subject to payment of the applicable Fees," and § 1.4 carves unaided-memory know-how out of Deliverables. Both are customary and sit above the fallback, so we are not opening § 14.
